claims.text: Pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder is prone to residual thermal stresses when processed under high thermal gradients.
Pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder is prone to microstructural inhomogeneity when processed under high thermal gradients.
Machine-learning-guided tuning can optimize the additive-manufacturing process parameters for this powder feedstock.
The combined pulsed-deposition, substrate-preheating, and localized-cryogenic-cooling regime can maintain an ultra-low thermal-input window.
The proposed processing window applies to miniature components with dimensions below a few centimeters.
The proposed process is applicable under an inert manufacturing atmosphere.
The combined intervention moderates the thermal gradient during deposition.
A moderated thermal gradient reduces thermal-stress accumulation.
Control of the thermal profile promotes a uniformly refined microstructure.
Pulsed energy deposition lowers peak melt-pool temperatures relative to continuous high-thermal-load processing.
Pulsed energy deposition minimizes thermal shock.
Controlled substrate preheating combined with localized cryogenic cooling creates a more stable thermal profile.
The proposed regime reduces residual stresses during rapid solidification.
The proposed regime produces a finer and more homogeneous grain structure.
Components made by the proposed regime will have statistically lower residual stresses than conventionally fabricated components.
Components made by the proposed regime will have greater tensile strength than conventionally fabricated components.
Components made by the proposed regime will have greater ductility than conventionally fabricated components.
Components made by the proposed regime will have a more uniform grain-size distribution than conventionally fabricated components.
Conventional continuous high-thermal-load additive manufacturing produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties in this alloy.
The proposed benefits are expected primarily in small-scale geometries.
